convention: s in [-1,+1]; -1 = position of the Democratic majority in Pew's Oct 2026 cross-tabs, +1 = Republican majority. The poll's convention, not ours. Order of axes carries no meaning.

weighting.name: horseshoe (operator, 2026-10-11)
weighting.statement: Any number can be lead. The horseshoe is just a weighting principle. People do not care about all issues.
weighting.definition: each molecule or ball carries an attention vector a on the simplex (sum 1). Its pillar is argmax a. Concentration h = a_max - 1/n (0 flat, (n-1)/n single-issue). Distance from molecule m to a point y: d_m(y) = sum_k a_mk |s_mk - y_k|. Changing the pillar re-ranks every distance; that is the horseshoe changing direction.

axes.name: Economy / safety net
neg: Government should expand programs like food assistance, disability, and welfare for people who need them.
Raising the minimum wage and taxing the wealthy more would make the economy fairer.
Public spending on social programs is an investment, not waste.
Corporations and the rich should pay a larger share of taxes.
Cutting the safety net hurts working families.
pos: Government spending is too high and should be cut.
Lower taxes and less regulation grow the economy for everyone.
Welfare programs should have work requirements and strict time limits.
The free market allocates resources better than government programs.
Deficits and the national debt are the biggest economic threat.

axes.name: Immigration
neg: Undocumented immigrants who work and pay taxes should get a path to legal status.
Mass deportation would be cruel and would damage the economy.
Immigrants strengthen the country.
Immigration enforcement raids on workplaces and neighborhoods go too far.
Asylum seekers deserve a fair hearing, not detention.
pos: The border must be secured before anything else is done on immigration.
People who entered the country illegally should be deported.
Illegal immigration drives up crime and drives down wages.
Sanctuary cities should lose federal funding.
Build the wall and enforce the laws already on the books.

axes.name: Healthcare
neg: Health care is a right and government should guarantee coverage for everyone.
Medicare should negotiate drug prices and be expanded.
The Affordable Care Act should be protected and strengthened.
A public option would lower costs for families.
No one should go bankrupt because they got sick.
pos: Government-run health care would mean rationing and long waits.
Health insurance should be left to the private market and competition.
The Affordable Care Act should be repealed.
Health savings accounts and price transparency beat government mandates.
People should not be forced to buy insurance.

axes.name: Education
neg: Public schools need more funding, not vouchers that drain them.
Teachers' unions protect educators and students.
Charter schools skim resources from neighborhood public schools.
Every child deserves a well-funded public school.
Education policy should be set by educators, not politicians.
pos: Parents should be able to choose charter schools, private schools, or home schooling with public money following the child.
Teachers' unions block reform and protect bad teachers.
School choice gives poor families the options rich families already have.
Public schools push ideology instead of teaching basics.
The federal Department of Education should be shut down.

axes.name: Foreign war / intervention
neg: The United States must keep arming and funding Ukraine against Russia.
America has a duty to defend democracies abroad.
Pulling back from our alliances would hand the world to dictators.
Military aid to allies is money well spent.
Isolationism made the last century's wars worse.
pos: Ukraine is not our war and we should stop sending money and weapons.
America should stop policing the world and fix problems at home.
Foreign aid and foreign wars drain money from American families.
The war in Ukraine should be ended by negotiation, including territorial concessions.
Regime change wars have failed everywhere we tried them.

axes.name: Abortion
neg: Abortion should be legal and the decision belongs to the woman and her doctor.
The government has no business in reproductive health decisions.
Overturning Roe v. Wade was wrong.
Abortion bans endanger women's lives.
Access to abortion is health care.
pos: Abortion ends a human life and should be illegal or tightly restricted.
The unborn child has a right to life.
States should be free to ban abortion.
Late-term abortion is indefensible.
Taxpayer money should never fund abortion.

axes.name: Guns
neg: We need universal background checks and a ban on assault weapons.
Gun violence is a public health crisis that stronger laws can reduce.
Red flag laws save lives.
No civilian needs a military-style rifle.
Gun manufacturers should be held liable for the harm their products do.
pos: The Second Amendment guarantees an individual right to own guns.
Gun control laws punish law-abiding owners and do not stop criminals.
More armed citizens make communities safer.
Gun registries are the first step toward confiscation.
Mental health, not guns, is the problem behind mass shootings.

notes: Seven axes (operator 2026-10-11: 'Maybe 6 is better. Or 7 is prime which allows a central issue'). Trade folded into the extended set; its stance is largely carried by the economy axis on these shows and is re-promotable.

The n=8 'spike' in kernel_field.py concerns the membrane Green's function in n dimensions, not the number of stance axes. Stance axes are measurement coordinates; the membrane runs on the 2-d base. Seven vs eight is free of that constraint.
Odd n gives a pillar with equal numbers of axes to either side when the operator wants to draw it that way; primality is not used by any formula.
